deposits.title: Machine-checked involution structure of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer functional equation and root number (Lean 4, axiom-free)
deposits.description:
NOT A NOVELTY CLAIM. This is a FORMALISATION of a known result: machine-checked in Lean 4, axiom-free, dated and citable. The prior art is cited in the references. No discovery is claimed.

A Lean 4 development of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer functional equation and root number: 5 theorems, each decided by the kernel with no axiom dependency and no Mathlib import. The propositions:

• Sigma is an involution — ∀ s ∈ [(-2 : Int), -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4], σ (σ s) = s
• Central point is the fixed point — σ 1 = 1 ∧ (∀ s ∈ [(-2 : Int), 0, 2, 3, 4], σ s ≠ s)
• Root number squares to one — (1 : Int) * 1 = 1 ∧ (-1 : Int) * (-1) = 1
• Root number one iff rank even — (∀ r ∈ [0, 2, 4, 6], sign r = 1) ∧ (∀ r ∈ [1, 3, 5, 7], sign r = -1)
• Parity is an involution — (∀ r ∈ [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5], sign (r + 1) = -(sign r)) ∧ (∀ r ∈ [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5], sign (r + 2) = sign r)

deposits.title: Machine-checked involution structure of a finite reflection, its fixed point and its vanishing resistance (Lean 4, axiom-free)
deposits.description:
NOT A NOVELTY CLAIM. This is a FORMALISATION of a known result: machine-checked in Lean 4, axiom-free, dated and citable. The prior art is cited in the references. No discovery is claimed.

A Lean 4 development of a finite reflection, its fixed point and its vanishing resistance: 9 theorems, each decided by the kernel with no axiom dependency and no Mathlib import. The propositions:

• The coin is an involution — ∀ d ∈ digits, σ (σ d) = d
• The harmonic is the only fixed point — digits.filter (fun d => σ d == d) = [5]
• All that is not harmonic is moved — (digits.filter (fun d => !(σ d == d))).length = 8
• The sides are equal and exchanged — below.length = above.length ∧ below.map σ = above.reverse ∧ above.map σ = below.reverse
• The coin is two sides and one edge — below.length + above.length + 1 = digits.length
• Every bit of resistance drains — ∀ d ∈ digits, resistance d + resistance (σ d) = 0
• The harmonic carries no resistance — resistance 5 = 0
• The whole surface sums to zero — (digits.map resistance).sum = 0
• The drain is exact at every scale — ∀ k ∈ [1, 10, 1000, 1000000], (digits.map (fun d => k * resistance d)).sum = 0

deposits.title: Machine-checked involution structure of involution (Lean 4, axiom-free)
deposits.description:
NOT A NOVELTY CLAIM. This is a FORMALISATION of a known result: machine-checked in Lean 4, axiom-free, dated and citable. The prior art is cited in the references. No discovery is claimed.

A Lean 4 development of involution: 8 theorems, each decided by the kernel with no axiom dependency and no Mathlib import. The propositions:

• Orbit sums to zero — {α : Type} (f : α → Int) (σ : α → α) (h : IsInvolution σ) (x : α) : odd f σ x + odd f σ (σ x) = 0
• Odd vanishes at a fixed point — {α : Type} (f : α → Int) (σ : α → α) (x : α) (hx : σ x = x) : odd f σ x = 0
• EvenPart is symmetric — {α : Type} (f : α → Int) (σ : α → α) (h : IsInvolution σ) (x : α) : evenPart f σ (σ x) = evenPart f σ x
• The split loses nothing — {α : Type} (f : α → Int) (σ : α → α) (x : α) : evenPart f σ x + odd f σ x = 2 * f x
• The instance is an involution — ∀ d ∈ carrier, σ (σ d) = d
• The instance cancels over every orbit — ∀ d ∈ carrier, (height d - height (σ d)) + (height (σ d) - height (σ (σ d))) = 0
• The instance has one harmonic point — carrier.filter (fun d => σ d == d) = [5]
• The instance splits without loss — ∀ d ∈ carrier, (height d + height (σ d)) + (height d - height (σ d)) = 2 * height d

priorArt.citation: classical linear algebra, the eigenspace decomposition of an involution: a linear involution on a vector space has eigenvalues ±1 and every element splits uniquely into its +1 (symmetric) and −1 (antisymmetric) parts. f(x) − f(σx) IS the antisymmetric part, and it cancels over every orbit because the two contributions differ only in sign. The same decomposition gives every square matrix as symmetric plus antisymmetric. Standard textbook material; the contribution here is the machine-checked statement, not the mathematics.

deposits.description:
NOT A NOVELTY CLAIM. This is a FORMALISATION of a known result: machine-checked in Lean 4, axiom-free, dated and citable. The prior art is cited in the references. No discovery is claimed.

A Lean 4 development of time reversal in the Euler and Navier–Stokes equations: 4 theorems, each decided by the kernel with no axiom dependency and no Mathlib import. The propositions:

• Reversal is an involution — T (T navierStokes) = navierStokes ∧ T (T euler) = euler
• Euler is time reversible — T euler = euler
• Viscosity breaks time reversal — T navierStokes ≠ navierStokes ∧ (T navierStokes).timeDerivative = navierStokes.timeDerivative ∧ (T navierStokes).convective = navierStokes.convective ∧ (T navierStokes).pressure = navierStokes.pressure ∧ (T navierStokes).viscous ≠ navierStokes.viscous
• Fixed points are exactly the inviscid — (∀ v ∈ [(-2 : Int), -1, 1, 2], T ⟨1,1,1,v⟩ ≠ ⟨1,1,1,v⟩) ∧ T ⟨1,1,1,0⟩ = ⟨1,1,1,0⟩

A Lean 4 development of spacetime: 7 theorems, each decided by the kernel with no axiom dependency and no Mathlib import. The propositions:
